stem:
A 10-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department after falling from his bike downhill into a parked car. He was thrown over the car, was not wearing a helmet, and was reportedly knocked unconscious. On arrival he has a large swelling over the right side of his head but no other obvious injuries. A rapid CT head scan is performed.

What is the most likely intracranial injury on CT?
explanation: A high-impact blunt head injury with a right-sided scalp swelling is most consistent with a right-sided extradural haematoma, classically due to temporal bone injury and middle meningeal artery bleeding.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency medicine - Trauma 3 - Head injury

optionExplanations.A: A skull fracture may coexist but does not best answer the question about the likely intracranial injury.
optionExplanations.B: Subdural haematomas are more often due to bridging vein injury and are less classically associated with this presentation.
optionExplanations.C: Subarachnoid haemorrhage can occur after trauma, but it is not the best fit here.
optionExplanations.D: Correct. A right-sided impact with focal scalp swelling and reduced consciousness is typical of a right extradural haematoma.
optionExplanations.E: The lesion would be expected on the same side as the impact, making a left extradural haematoma unlikely.

source.questionTextHtml:
After reassessing Johnny's ABCDEs and ensuring he is as stable as possible, you assist in transferring him for a CT scan. The scan is performed rapidly, producing the accompanying image.

Which one of the following is shown in the CT scan?

Clinical scenario 1 - Johnny

Teaching/Learning points:

Rapid neurological assessment

GCS including AVPU and Modified GCS

Prevention of secondary insult

Johnny is a 10 year old boy. He is en-route to the emergency department via ambulance following a fall from his bike. Paramedics have called ahead, stating Johnny was riding downhill and hit the side of a parked car at the bottom. He was thrown over the car, landing on the street. He was not wearing a helmet and was apparently knocked unconscious.

He is described as semi-conscious, breathing at a rate of 18/min, sats 98% in air, heart rate 90pbm. He has a large swelling to the right side of his head, and no other obvious injuries. Their ETA is 15 minutes.

The following ten questions refer to Johnny’s clinical scenario.
